hero.title: Erectile dysfunction
hero.summary: Get confidential care for difficulty getting or keeping an erection. Understand causes, tests, treatment options, and follow-up.

body: Erectile dysfunction means difficulty getting or keeping an erection firm enough for sex. It is common and treatable.
ED can be linked to diabetes, blood pressure, heart health, stress, anxiety, low testosterone, medicines, smoking, alcohol, obesity, sleep problems, or nerve and blood flow issues.

subsections.title: Symptoms
body: Symptoms include getting an erection sometimes but not every time, losing erection too early, weak erection, reduced confidence, or no erection.
ED may also occur with low desire, early ejaculation, urinary symptoms, or fertility concerns.

subsections.title: When to consult a urologist
body: Consult a urologist if erection difficulty lasts more than a few weeks, affects confidence, affects relationship, or happens with diabetes, blood pressure, or heart risk.
You should also consult before taking pills on your own, especially if you use heart medicines or nitrates.

subsections.title: Diagnosis and tests
body: Evaluation may include medical history, sexual history, medicine review, physical examination, blood sugar, lipid profile, testosterone, thyroid tests, and other tests when needed.
Patients also need to be evaluated from the cardiac point of view to exclude coronary artery disease.
The aim is to treat the cause and improve sexual function safely.

experience.title: Treatment options for erectile dysfunction
body: ED treatment is personal. It should be safe, private, and matched to the cause.
Options may include lifestyle changes, medicines, hormone treatment, counseling support, vacuum devices, injections, or penile implant discussion in selected cases.

items.question: Is ED a normal part of aging?
items.answer: ED becomes more common with age, but it is not something you have to ignore.

items.question: Can diabetes cause ED?
items.answer: Yes. Diabetes can affect blood vessels and nerves that help erections.

items.question: Can I take ED pills without a doctor?
items.answer: It is safer to consult first, especially if you take heart medicines or nitrates.

items.question: Can stress cause ED?
items.answer: Yes. Stress, anxiety, sleep issues, and relationship concerns can contribute.

items.question: Is treatment confidential?
items.answer: Yes. ED concerns are handled privately and respectfully.
